findings.description: Unsafe pickle deserialization in cache metadata loading allows arbitrary code execution
findings.reasoning: The _load method in CacheMetadata class uses pickle.load() without any validation or sanitization. The method first attempts to load JSON, and if that fails (ValueError), it falls back to pickle.load(). This allows an attacker to craft a malicious pickle file that will be deserialized when cache metadata is loaded, leading to arbitrary code execution. The pickle module is known to be unsafe for loading untrusted data as it can execute arbitrary Python code during deserialization.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: The _load method is called from load() method (line 160) and save() method (line 202). Both methods get file paths from _scan_locations() which appears to scan cache directory locations. An attacker with write access to cache directories or who can influence file paths could place malicious pickle files that would be loaded.
evidence.notes: This is a classic CWE-502 vulnerability. Pickle should never be used to load untrusted data. The code should either: 1) Remove pickle support entirely and only use JSON, 2) Use a safe deserialization library, or 3) Implement proper validation and signature checking for pickle files.
